chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, VerseEnd Verse2 to the saints and faithful brethren in Christ who are at Colosse: Grace be unto you, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd

Verse3 We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you VerseEnd Verse4 since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of your love which you have to all the saints, VerseEnd Verse5 for the hope which is laid up for you in Heaven, whereof you heard before in the word of the truth of the gospel, VerseEnd Verse6 which has come unto you as in all generations of the world and brings forth fruit, as it does also in you, since the day you heard of it and knew the grace of God in truth VerseEnd Verse7 as you also learned of Epaphras, our dear fellow servant who is for you a faithful minister of Christ, VerseEnd Verse8 who also declared unto us your love in the spirit. VerseEnd

Verse9 For this cause, we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you and to desire that you might be filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, VerseEnd Verse10 that you might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing: being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God, VerseEnd Verse11 strengthened with all might according to his glorious power unto all patience and long-suffering with joyfulness, VerseEnd Verse12 giving thanks unto the Father, who has made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light, VerseEnd Verse13 who has delivered us from the power of darkness and has translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son VerseEnd — Verse14 in whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins VerseEnd — Verse15 who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature. VerseEnd

Verse16 For by him were all things created that are in heaven and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they are thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers. All things were created by him and for him, VerseEnd Verse17 and he is before all things, and by him all things consist. VerseEnd Verse18 And he is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things he might have the preeminence. VerseEnd Verse19 For it pleased the Father that in him should all fullness dwell, VerseEnd Verse20 and having made peace through the blood of his cross by him, to reconcile all things unto himself by him, I say, whether they are things in earth or things in Heaven. VerseEnd

Verse21 And you that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now has he reconciled VerseEnd Verse22 in the body of his flesh, through death, to present you holy and blameless and unreproveable in his sight VerseEnd Verse23 if you continue in the faith, grounded and settled, and are not moved away from the hope of the gospel which you have heard, and which was preached to every creature which is under Heaven whereof I, Paul, am made a minister, VerseEnd Verse24 who now rejoices in my sufferings for you and fills up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh, for his body’s sake — which is the church VerseEnd — Verse25 whereof I am made a minister according to the dispensation of God which is given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God, VerseEnd Verse26 even the mystery which has been hidden from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints, VerseEnd Verse27 to whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ, in you, the hope of glory, VerseEnd Verse28 whom we preach, warning every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus, VerseEnd Verse29 for which I also labor, striving according to his working, which works in me mightily. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 For I wish that you knew what great conflict I have, for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh, VerseEnd Verse2 that their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of Christ, who is of God, even the Father, VerseEnd Verse3 in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. VerseEnd Verse4 And this I say lest any man should beguile you with enticing words, VerseEnd Verse5 for though I am absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, rejoicing and beholding your order, and the steadfastness of your faith in Christ. VerseEnd Verse6 As you have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him, VerseEnd Verse7 rooted and built up in him, and established in the faith as you have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving. VerseEnd

Verse8 Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ; VerseEnd Verse9 for in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily. VerseEnd Verse10 And you are complete in him who is the head of all principality and power, VerseEnd Verse11 in whom also you are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ, VerseEnd Verse12 buried with him in baptism, wherein you are also risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who has raised him from the dead. VerseEnd

Verse13 And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, has he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses, VerseEnd Verse14 blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us — which was contrary to us — and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. VerseEnd Verse15 And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it. VerseEnd

Verse16 Let no man therefore judge you in food or in drink, or in respect of a holy day, or of the new moon, or of the Sabbath days, VerseEnd Verse17 which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. VerseEnd Verse18 Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he has not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind, VerseEnd Verse19 and not holding the Head, from which all the body, by joints and bands having nourishment ministered and knit together, increases with the increase of God. VerseEnd

Verse20 Wherefore, if you are dead with Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as though living in the world, are you subject to ordinances VerseEnd Verse21 which are after the doctrines and commandments of men who teach you to touch not, taste not, handle not VerseEnd Verse22 all those things which are to perish with the using? VerseEnd — Verse23 which things have indeed a show of wisdom in self-willed worship, and humility, and neglecting the body as to the satisfying the flesh — not in any honor to God. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 If you then are risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sits on the right hand of God. VerseEnd Verse2 Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth; VerseEnd Verse3 for you are dead, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. VerseEnd Verse4 When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall you also appear with him in glory. VerseEnd

Verse5 Put to death therefore your members which are upon the earth: fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil lust, and covetousness, which is idolatry, VerseEnd Verse6 for which things’ sake the wrath of God comes on the children of disobedience, VerseEnd Verse7 in which you also walked sometime when you lived in them. VerseEnd Verse8 But now also put off all these: anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, filthy communication out of your mouth. VerseEnd Verse9 Lie not one to another, seeing that you have put off the old man — with his deeds VerseEnd — Verse10 and have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him, VerseEnd Verse11 where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcised nor uncircumcised, foreigner, Scythian, bond nor free, but Christ is all and in all. VerseEnd

Verse12 Put on therefore as the elect of God, holy and beloved, hearts of mercies, kindness, humility of mind, meekness, long-suffering, VerseEnd Verse13 bearing with one another and forgiving one another. If any man have a quarrel against any, even as Christ forgave you, so also do you; VerseEnd Verse14 and above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness. VerseEnd Verse15 And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you are called in one body. And be thankful. VerseEnd Verse16 Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another in psalms, and hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. VerseEnd Verse17 And whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him. VerseEnd

Verse18 Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord. VerseEnd Verse19 Husbands, love your wives and be not bitter against them. VerseEnd Verse20 Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well-pleasing unto the VerseEnd Verse21 Lord. Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they VerseEnd should be discouraged.

Verse22 Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh — not with eye-service, as men-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God. VerseEnd Verse23 And whatever you do, do it heartily as to the Lord and not unto men, VerseEnd Verse24 knowing that of the Lord you shall receive the reward of the inheritance, for you serve the Lord Christ. VerseEnd Verse25 But he that does wrong shall receive for the wrong which he has done, and there is no respect of persons. VerseEnd LEChapter4 Verse1 Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal, knowing that you also have a Master in Heaven. VerseEnd

Verse2 Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving, VerseEnd Verse3 at the same time praying also for us, that God would open unto us a door of utterance to speak the mystery of Christ (for which I am also in bonds) VerseEnd, Verse4 that I may make it manifest as I ought to speak. VerseEnd Verse5 Walk in wisdom toward them that are outside, redeeming the time. VerseEnd Verse6 Let your speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer every man. VerseEnd

Verse7 All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, VerseEnd Verse8 whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose — that he might know your estate and comfort your hearts VerseEnd Verse9 with Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here. VerseEnd Verse10 Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, salutes you; and Mark, sister’s son to Barnabas (concerning whom you received commandments — if he come unto you, receive him) VerseEnd; Verse11 and Jesus, who is called Justus, who are of the circumcision. These only are my fellow workers in the kingdom of God, who have been a comfort unto me. VerseEnd Verse12 Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, salutes you, always laboring fervently for you in prayers that you may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God; VerseEnd Verse13 for I bear him record, that he has a great zeal for you, and them who are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis. VerseEnd Verse14 Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you. VerseEnd

Verse15 Salute the brethren who are in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church which is in his house. VerseEnd Verse16 And when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you likewise read the epistle from Laodicea. VerseEnd Verse17 And say to Archippus, Take heed to the ministry which you have received in the Lord, that you fulfill it. VerseEnd
Verse18 The salutation by the hand of me, Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: Written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus.
